svg.text: Everyday English - Idioms & slang
keep your eyes on the ball
MEANING
To remain focused on the most important aspect of a
situation.
SYNONYMS
stay focused on the objective; avoid losing sight of
the goal
IN CONTEXT
We have many small tasks, but we must keep our
eyes on the ball: the final launch date.
USAGE NOTE
This sports metaphor can encourage focus, but an
imperative from a manager may imply that someone
has been inattentive. Inclusive "let us keep our eyes
on the ball" shares responsibility; "keep your eyes
on the ball" can sound like a rebuke. Judge the
relationship and tone.
CONVERSATION
A: The manager told me to keep my eyes on the
ball.
B: Did it sound supportive or critical?
A: Critical; she said it after I missed a deadline.
B: In that context, it implies your attention slipped.
YOUR TURN
A colleague missed a detail. Rewrite "Keep your eyes
on the ball" to share responsibility. Model: Let us
keep our eyes on the ball and check the launch risks
together.
